title: Natural gas leak
tldr: If you smell gas or suspect a leak, leave the area on foot immediately. Do not use switches, flames, phones or engines in the suspected leak area. Once safely away, call emergency services and your gas utility. Do not reenter until cleared.
steps: Do not search for the leak or stop to collect belongings.
Do not turn electrical devices on or off, light flames, operate garage doors or start a vehicle nearby.
Give the address and what you noticed to emergency services and the utility.
Wait outside the danger area and follow responder instructions.
next: Have the utility or a qualified technician restore service and inspect appliances when required.
watch: Never use a flame to test for leaks or attempt your own repair.
review_status: source-linked editorial review; not independent expert certification
without_help: Stay outside and away even if the utility line is busy. Keep others from entering without approaching the leak. A lack of response does not make reentry safe; use another place to stay until the hazard has been assessed by qualified personnel.
household: Choose an outside meeting place and check that every person can use the escape route. Keep keys, mobility aids and shoes accessible. Tell neighbours about a hazard from a safe location; do not organise an untrained entry or rescue.
pack_now: Keep essential medicines, drinking water, a battery light, shoes, phone power and a written contact card within reach. Adapt the load to the hazard and the people with you; do not delay escape to collect equipment.
